transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood CSM); Leah Patel (Procurement), Dr. Omar Basu (Head of AI), Mina Lopes (Legal), Samir Nadeem (Security, partial)

Summary: seen above (auto)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, AE for Redwood. We have Mateo on the line to go through the technical notes and Jordan to capture onboarding steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Leah Patel: Good, thanks. Sorry for being a little early, procurement prep meeting ran long.
[00:12] Dr. Omar Basu: Hi, Omar here. We're mainly focused on the pricing exception that procurement flagged and some questions on privileged access for our private deployment.
[00:20] Ava Chen: Great, that aligns. Mateo, wanna take the pricing and pilot run overview, then we can dig into DPA/MSA redlines and KMS?
[00:26] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. Quick clarifying note — when we say pricing exception here, we're talking about a short-term reserved capacity discount for the dedicated GPU pool, yes? Not, like, permanent net-new contract terms.
[00:34] Leah Patel: Correct. Procurement asked if we can lock a 12‑month commit at a lower per-token effective rate during the pilot phase. There's also a request to classify a tranche as "privileged" with narrower access controls.
[00:46] Mateo Ruiz: Understood. For dedicated, we can map a committed QPS bucket and offer a tiered discount; the ask for privileged tranche usually affects our onboarding and keying — KMS, HSM access, RBAC, that stack.
[00:56] Mina Lopes: On the legal side, we need clarity on data flows. Our DPA team flagged the log retention clause and the privileged access wording in the onboarding docs; also want to see KMS controls spelled out (bring back conversation to regulatory constraints for our clinical dataset).
[01:12] Ava Chen: Thanks Mina. We'll prep a DPA redline and security pack. Quick note: our standard DPA allows customer-managed keys in Private deployments but there are nuances with on-prem HSM vs cloud KMS.
[01:24] Samir Nadeem: Sorry I'm late — joined now. From security: we care about key escrow, separation of duties, and auditability. Do you support HSM-backed keys in the private control plane?
[01:34] Mateo Ruiz: Short answer: yes but depends on deployment mode. For VPC Private, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) and can support external HSMs via KMIP or vendor-specific connectors. For on-prem, HSM integration is possible but requires a runbook and network setup.
[01:51] Leah Patel: That sounds OK. The procurement committee also asked whether Redwood can add a clause for privileged access approvals — basically a seven‑day notification and two‑party sign-off before any elevated session.
[02:04] Jordan Park: From onboarding perspective, we can implement an approval workflow: request -> audit trail -> time-limited access. Our consoles support role-based entitlements, but the legal text needs to align with operational capabilities.
[02:18] Dr. Omar Basu: On performance: we want some baseline numbers. Our internal SLA target is 90th percentile < 120ms for short prompts, and throughput enough to support 50 concurrent sessions. Can Redwood guarantee that on the dedicated profile?
[02:33] Mateo Ruiz: The dedicated pool SLA is throughput-based; latency guarantees depend on model choice, sequence length distribution, and whether KV caching is enabled. We can run a benchmark in a reserved test pool and produce 90/95/99 percentiles. The pilot will show if we hit your 120ms target for the model family you pick.
[02:50] Mina Lopes: If the pilot doesn't meet SLA, what are our remediation/levers? Credit? Right of termination?
[02:58] Ava Chen: Standard playbook: SLA credits for verified breaches, and contractual remedies in the MSA. For enterprise customers we can negotiate stronger SLAs in Dedicated agreements; that will be part of procurement discussion.
[03:09] Leah Patel: Procurement will want specific SLA credit numbers to present to finance — e.g., x% credits for y minutes of downtime or for sustained latency above threshold.
[03:18] Mateo Ruiz: We'll draft an SLA appendix showing credit tiering and an objective test harness for the benchmark.
[03:23] [crosstalk — brief]
[03:26] Samir Nadeem: On KMS: Is there an approach for split keys? We cannot have Redwood hold full key material.
[03:31] Mateo Ruiz: We support customer-managed keys and key-wrapping so Redwood never has plaintext key material. In Private on VPC we can integrate with your KMS and also use envelope encryption. For split keys/smaller vaults, that's more of an HSM design thing — we can explore a KMIP-based connector.
[03:47] Dr. Omar Basu: Good. Also, how auditable are admin sessions? We need session recordings or at least keystroke-level audit?
[03:55] Jordan Park: We can provide detailed audit logs, session IDs, time-bounded elevated access, and per-token tracing metadata. Full keystroke recording is not something we usually do, but we can capture command logs and actions. We'll include the audit log retention policy in the security pack.
[04:12] Mina Lopes: Please note retention limits — some regs require 7 years for clinical research logs, others less; we'll specify which ones apply.
[04:20] Ava Chen: Good call. We'll ask you to enumerate applicable regs and we will mark the parts of the security pack that meet them.
[04:26] [00:04:30] Mateo Ruiz: Back to pricing exception — high level: if you sign a 12-month commit for X GPUs equivalent, we can give a staged discount: 10% off year one, with a review for year two. There's also a one-time onboarding discount we can apply. I will attach the math to the spreadsheet.
[04:46] Leah Patel: Procurement's ask includes a carve-out where a small percentage (say 10%) of capacity is marked privileged and billed at a different rate with stricter entitlements. Can Redwood do tiered billing inside the same committed pool?
[04:58] Mateo Ruiz: Yes we can logically partition capacity and apply different entitlements and routes — it's a config on the orchestration layer. Billing-wise we can produce separate cost centers for those partitions. We'll show an example in the worksheet.
[05:10] Dr. Omar Basu: Any gotchas around fallback — like if privileged tranche spikes, will Redwood automatically evict non-privileged traffic? We need predictable behavior.
[05:20] Mateo Ruiz: We have routing policies. For dedicated pools we can configure priority and preemption policies. For a strict SLA you'd want capacity guardrails and some buffer headroom; we'll recommend commit margin for your worst-case.
[05:33] Mina Lopes: On the DPA side: one redline we will push is audit log access — who at Redwood can view logs for Private? We need to limit that and require 2FA and documented approvals.
[05:45] Ava Chen: Understood. Our security pack will outline admin roles, mandatory 2FA, and approval workflow. For Private deployments, customers can opt for no-Redwood-admin mode but that increases onboarding complexity.
[05:58] Leah Patel: That option might actually be preferable — procurement will take that to the committee. It may affect pricing though.
[06:05] Ava Chen: It does — fully customer-controlled admin entails more custom enablement and higher setup fees; we'll show both options in the pricing worksheet.
[06:13] [00:06:20] Jordan Park: Quick operational note: onboarding timeline for Dedicated + private keying is typically 4–6 weeks once terms are agreed — that includes network setup, HSM integration if needed, and a bench. We'll list out milestones in the checklist.
[06:29] Leah Patel: Timeline seems reasonable. For procurement approval, we need to know fiscal impact and any termination liability tied to the pricing exception.
[06:37] Mateo Ruiz: We'll add a simple model: committed spend per month, effective rate after discount, and early termination fee schedule.
[06:45] Mina Lopes: Regarding privileged access clause language: we will add suggested wording and want a clause that requires notification and a named approver — we'll share a sample redline after this call.
[06:56] Ava Chen: Perfect. We'll then incorporate into the MSA appendix.
[07:00] [00:07:05] Leah Patel: Any other vendor concerns? We did ask about competitor comparisons earlier — we looked at Anthropic's enterprise offering and OpenAI's dedicated endpoints. One question is around data residency and the ability to keep all logs within our tenancy.
[07:18] Mateo Ruiz: For Private deployments, logs and data reside in your VPC; Redwood's control plane can be configured to minimize copies. For hosted we do have cross-region replication for resilience, which may not suit you. We'll make that explicit in the security pack.
[07:31] Dr. Omar Basu: OK. On the benchmark: can you run our representative prompts and include tokenization differences? Our prompts are long-ish, 500–800 tokens per request on average.
[07:42] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we'll run sequence-length matched tests. Please send a sanitized sample prompt set; we'll run tests under the same model and sequence distribution.
[07:51] Leah Patel: We'll sanitize and send by end of day Thursday.
[07:55] Ava Chen: Thanks. Recap then: Redwood to send security pack, DPA redlines, reserved-cap pricing worksheet with privileged tranche example, and an SLA appendix. Saffron to send sanitized prompt set, legal comments on DPA, and procurement will route pricing exception.
[08:10] Mina Lopes: One small thing — can Redwood provide a granular entitlements export so our IAM team can map SAML groups?
[08:17] Jordan Park: Yes, we'll provide an entitlements mapping CSV and sample SAML assertions.
[08:22] Leah Patel: Great. That should help procurement and security sign-off.
[08:27] Ava Chen: Any last questions?
[08:29] Samir Nadeem: None from security beyond what we noted. We'll review the security pack and follow up.
[08:33] Dr. Omar Basu: No further items. Thanks.
[08:36] Ava Chen: Thanks all. We'll aim to get the docs out by Dec 7 and the pilot scheduled week of Dec 13. Jordan will send the onboarding checklist.
[08:44] Leah Patel: Appreciate it.
[08:46] Ava Chen: Alright, closing. Bye.

--- End transcript ---
